activate_when: A material feature or fix is ready for implementation against an established architecture
Implementation crosses one or more meaningful repository or system boundaries
The agent must preserve authoritative ownership and repository conventions while changing behavior
capabilities.description: Implement features and fixes through the repository's chosen architecture, preserving authoritative boundaries and contracts while making the smallest maintainable change that satisfies acceptance criteria.
inputs: applicable project instructions and verification surfaces
capabilities.purpose: Implement accepted behavior through the authoritative project architecture with minimal maintainable change, preserving contracts and implementation freedom without generic stack mandates.

activate_when: A material implementation has a coherent repository diff ready for senior review
The actual changed files may differ from the original plan or introduce hidden release implications
The agent must validate correctness, architecture fit, scope, evidence, and maintainability before completion
capabilities.description: Review the actual repository diff like a skeptical senior engineer, checking correctness, architecture fit, regressions, scope, maintainability, and evidence before a change is treated as release-ready.
capabilities.purpose: Review the actual code diff like a skeptical senior engineer, prioritizing correctness and project-specific risk over stylistic churn before final verification.

activate_when: A project uses runtime configuration, credentials, or external services
Local/test/preview/production environments need explicit separation
Deployment can fail or expose secrets if configuration remains implicit
capabilities.description: Design and verify safe, explicit runtime configuration across local, test, preview/staging, and production environments, keeping secrets out of source and making missing or invalid configuration fail clearly.
capabilities.purpose: Make runtime configuration explicit and safe across environments while keeping secrets out of source/evidence and avoiding unnecessary credential-related blocking.

activate_when: A material change requires sequencing across multiple engineering units
Unknowns or dependencies make direct editing likely to create rework
Acceptance criteria need to trace into implementation and verification
capabilities.description: Build a proportionate, repository-aware implementation plan from acceptance criteria, sequencing the smallest safe change and its evidence without pretending uncertain file-level details are known.
capabilities.purpose: Plan the smallest safe repository-aware path from accepted outcome to verified implementation while preserving flexibility under new evidence.

activate_when: A new product or major capability begins from a rough idea or outcome request
The user has not supplied a professional product brief
A proposed technical solution may be standing in for an unstated underlying problem
capabilities.description: Turn a rough product idea or outcome request into a clear problem, user, success, constraint, and non-goal frame before architecture or implementation begins, while avoiding unnecessary product ceremony for small changes.
capabilities.purpose: Turn rough product intent into a compact, decision-aware problem and outcome frame so engineering solves the right problem without forcing a non-expert user to author a PRD.

activate_when: A greenfield architecture has been chosen and the project repository must be initialized
An existing empty/minimal repository lacks executable engineering foundations
Bootstrap decisions must remain compatible with the intended deployment model
capabilities.description: Create the smallest maintainable greenfield repository foundation implied by the chosen architecture, including project structure, executable verification surfaces, configuration conventions, and developer guidance without speculative infrastructure.
capabilities.purpose: Create the smallest maintainable project foundation required by the chosen architecture without speculative tooling or infrastructure.

activate_when: Material work in an unfamiliar existing repository
The responsible files or architecture boundary are not yet clear
Repository conventions should determine the implementation approach
capabilities.description: Map an unfamiliar or materially relevant existing repository before changing it, finding the smallest architecture, conventions, tests, and change surface needed for the task.
capabilities.purpose: Map the smallest relevant portion of an existing repository before material change, grounding implementation choices in actual project architecture and conventions.

activate_when: User intent is outcome-oriented but not yet testable
Material behavior has multiple plausible interpretations
Completion criteria must distinguish explicit requirements from engineering inferences
capabilities.description: Turn user intent and repository context into testable acceptance criteria, separating explicit requirements, justified engineering inferences, assumptions, and decisions that genuinely require the user.
capabilities.purpose: Turn user intent and project evidence into a scoped, observable acceptance contract without forcing users to specify inferable engineering details.

activate_when: A greenfield product needs system boundaries and a technology stack before implementation
A material architecture change has several plausible technical options
Deployment or operational constraints can materially change the right design
capabilities.description: Choose proportionate system boundaries and technology stack from product requirements, project constraints, operational reality, ecosystem maturity, and deployment needs rather than habit or trend.
capabilities.purpose: Choose a simple, defensible architecture and stack from project evidence rather than habit, while incorporating deployment and operational reality from the start.

activate_when: A failure exists but its root cause is not established
Several plausible causes require evidence to discriminate
An intermittent or cross-layer defect needs a controlled diagnosis
capabilities.description: Diagnose non-obvious failures by reproducing the symptom, separating facts from hypotheses, narrowing the causal path with discriminating experiments, and fixing the smallest verified root cause.
capabilities.purpose: Diagnose non-obvious failures through causal evidence and discriminating experiments before applying the narrowest verified fix.

activate_when: Fixing a reproducible defect
Changing observable behavior where repository-native executable evidence can be written first
Preventing a regression with a focused behavioral test
capabilities.description: Establish executable behavioral evidence before fixing bugs or changing testable behavior, using the repository's existing test surfaces and proportionate RED-GREEN-refactor discipline rather than universal coverage or tooling rules.
capabilities.purpose: Establish executable evidence around defects and testable behavior changes using proportionate repository-native TDD rather than universal tooling or coverage rules.

activate_when: A material change appears complete and the completion claim needs evidence
The actual diff may have introduced verification obligations beyond the original plan
A distinction is needed between implemented, deployable, deployed, and post-deploy verified
capabilities.description: Verify that the evidence actually supports the completion claim before saying work is done. Use after implementation, debugging, refactoring, or any material change, and distinguish code-complete, deployable, deployed, and post-deploy-verified states.
capabilities.purpose: Ensure completion claims do not exceed actual evidence by verifying the changed behavior with proportionate repository-native checks and explicit claim boundaries.
